title: Food Safety Knowledge and Microbiological Risk Associated with Staphylococcus aureus: Evidence from Peruvian Restaurants
content: Background/Objectives: Food safety knowledge is a component of risk prevention in food service settings, but it should be assessed alongside microbiological indicators. This study examined the association between knowledge of food hygiene and handling and microbiological non-compliance for Staphylococcus aureus among food handlers in restaurants in Lima, Peru. Methods: A quantitative, observational, non-experimental study comprising two assessments conducted in 2022–2024 was carried out. Each assessment included 450 records from food handlers in 170 restaurants. Knowledge was assessed using 20 questions. Eight experts reviewed the instrument (Ai-ken’s V = 0.85775), and its internal consistency coefficients were 0.7791 and 0.7509, respectively. Microbiological results were classified according to Peruvian Ministerial Resolution No. 461-2007/MINSA: counts below 100 CFU/hands indicated compliance, whereas counts of 100 CFU/hands or higher indicated non-compliance. Frequencies were calculated, and Spearman’s correlation coefficient was used. Results: In the first assessment, 60.67% of participants were classified as failing and 1.56% as very good. In the second assessment, these proportions were 15.56% and 53.56%, respectively. Microbiological non-compliance was observed in 136/450 records (30.22%) in the first assessment and 72/450 (16.00%) in the second. Knowledge was inversely associated with microbiological non-compliance, with a moderate association in the first assessment (ρ = −0.520; p < 0.001) and a very strong association in the second (ρ = −0.983; p < 0.001). Conclusions: Given the observational design, the use of different question sets, and the lack of confirmed individual-level matching of records, differences between assessments were interpreted descriptively rather than causally. Combining knowledge assessment with microbiological findings offers a complementary approach to food safety surveillance in restaurants.
